explanation:
## What the grid is made of

Every input has two kinds of things on a blank (0) background:

- **Single red (2) cells** arranged on a regular lattice: they sit on a few fixed rows and a few fixed columns (e.g. rows 1, 6, 11 and columns 1, 6, 11 in pair 1). These never move — the fact sheet shows every red cell is identical in input and output.
- **Small blue (1) shapes** of 3 or 4 cells (2×2 squares and L-tromino shapes), each one living inside one "cell" of that lattice, i.e. between two consecutive marker rows and two consecutive marker columns.

The changed cells are all blue going to 0 or 0 going to blue, and every output blue shape has the same cell pattern as some input blue shape, just shifted by one or two cells. So the shapes are **moved, not reshaped**.

## Where do they move to?

Compare the positions. In pair 1 the shape with bbox rows 2–3 / cols 2–3 ends up at rows 3–4 / cols 3–4. The surrounding markers are rows 1 and 6 and columns 1 and 6, so the free interior is rows 2..5 and cols 2..5 (4 cells wide). A 2-cell-tall shape centred in rows 2..5 occupies rows 3–4; likewise cols 3–4. That is exactly the output.

The same holds for every shape: each blue shape is slid to the **centre of its lattice cell**, keeping its own pattern. With a 4-wide gap and 2-wide shapes the centring is exact; the formula I use is `top = lower_marker + 1 + (gap - height) // 2`, which handles any width. In pair 3 the markers are at columns 0 and 5, so the gap is cols 1..4 and the 2-wide shapes land at cols 2–3 — again matching the output (the shape that starts at cols 1–2 moves right by one, the one at cols 3–4 moves left by one, the ones already at cols 7–8 past the last marker column stay put because there is no marker on their right to centre against).

I coded this and checked it against all three train pairs in the inspect call above: every output was reproduced exactly.

## How the markers and shapes are found generically

- Background = most common colour.
- The marker colour is the colour whose objects are all single cells (red here, but derived from the grid).
- Marker rows / columns are the sets of rows / columns containing any marker cell.
- Every other object is a shape to be re-centred: find the nearest marker row at or above its centre and the nearest one below, centre vertically in that gap; same horizontally. If a shape has no marker on one side, it keeps its coordinate on that axis.

## Applying it to the test input

The test grid (17×13) has markers at rows 1, 6, 11, 16 and columns 2, 7, 12, so each lattice cell is a 4×4 interior (rows 2..5, 7..10, 12..15; cols 3..6, 8..11). The six blue shapes get centred:

- the 2×2 at rows 4–5 / cols 3–4 → rows 3–4 / cols 4–5;
- the L at rows 4–5 / cols 9–10 → rows 3–4 / cols 9–10 (already centred horizontally, moves up one);
- the L at rows 7–8 / cols 10–11 → rows 8–9 / cols 9–10;
- the 2×2 at rows 9–10 / cols 4–5 → already centred, stays;
- the L at rows 12–13 / cols 9–10 → rows 13–14 / cols 9–10;
- the L at rows 13–14 / cols 4–5 → rows 13–14 / cols 4–5, stays.

The emitted stages are: first the canvas with only the markers kept (all shapes cleared), then one stage per shape as it is stamped into its centred position.
code:
def transform(grid):
    g = np.array(grid)
    bg = background(g)
    objs = objects(g, bg)
    from collections import defaultdict
    sizes = defaultdict(list)
    for o in objs:
        sizes[o["colour"]].append(o["size"])
    # marker colour: the colour whose objects are all single cells
    mc = [c for c, s in sizes.items() if max(s) == 1][0]
    ys, xs = np.where(g == mc)
    rows = sorted(set(ys.tolist()))
    cols = sorted(set(xs.tolist()))

    out = np.full_like(g, bg)
    out[g == mc] = mc
    emit(out.copy(), "Keep the single-cell marker lattice; clear every shape so it can be re-placed.")

    def place(markers, c0, c1):
        h = c1 - c0 + 1
        cen = (c0 + c1) / 2
        lo = max([m for m in markers if m <= cen], default=None)
        hi = min([m for m in markers if m > cen], default=None)
        if lo is None or hi is None:
            return c0
        return lo + 1 + (hi - lo - 1 - h) // 2

    for o in objs:
        if o["colour"] == mc:
            continue
        y0, x0, y1, x1 = o["box"]
        ty = place(rows, y0, y1)
        tx = place(cols, x0, x1)
        for y, x in o["cells"]:
            out[y - y0 + ty, x - x0 + tx] = o["colour"]
        emit(out.copy(), f"Shape at rows {y0}-{y1}, cols {x0}-{x1} slid to the centre of its lattice cell: rows {ty}-{ty+y1-y0}, cols {tx}-{tx+x1-x0}.")

    emit(out.copy(), "All shapes centred between their surrounding markers.")
    return out
